concerns.text: T009a and T009b are listed as [P] (parallel-safe) but both write to the same output file `results/target_imbalance_scores.csv` (T009a) and `results/compositional_imbalance_score.csv` (T009b). T009a writes to the same file as T008. T008 and T009a have identical descriptions and output paths, creating a race condition if run in parallel. T009a must be removed or merged with T008, and T009b must not run until T008/T009a complete if they share state.

T012, T014, and T020 are marked [P] (parallel-safe) but all depend on T010b (schema generation). The 'Dependencies' section explicitly states T010b must complete before these tasks. Marking them [P] implies they can run immediately or in parallel with each other without T010b, which is false. They must be unmarked [P] or T010b must be moved to Phase 1.

T019 depends on T012 and T013 passing. T012 is marked [~] (incomplete) and T013 is [X]. T019 is marked [P] but cannot run until T012 completes. This violates the producer-consumer flow where the test artifact (T012) must exist before the verification task (T019) can execute.
T029 depends on T028 (reading `results/power_analysis.json`). T028 is marked [~] (incomplete). T029 is marked [P] but cannot run until T028 produces the artifact. This is a hidden ordering violation.

T030 and T031 depend on T027 (`results/performance_degradation.csv`). T027 is marked [~] (incomplete). T030 and T031 are marked [P] but cannot run until T027 completes. This violates the producer-consumer flow.

T042 depends on T034 and T035. T034 and T035 are marked [ ] (not started). T042 is marked [P] but cannot run until T034/T035 complete.
T047 depends on T016, T027, and T030. T016, T027, and T030 are marked [~] or [ ] (incomplete/not started). T047 is marked [P] but cannot run until these artifacts are generated.

T009a and T009b descriptions are nearly identical to T008 and T009b respectively, causing confusion. T008 and T009a both claim to output to `results/target_imbalance_scores.csv`. This suggests a duplication error in task definition rather than a true parallel opportunity.
